past trauma exposure is associated with negative behavioral and clinical HIV outcomes, even after accounting for psychosocial mediatiors.
trauma was associated with 6 of the 7 behavioral or health outcomes we assessed, but that these relationships were only partially mediated by the psychosocial factors we considered.

trauma exposure was associated with several negative outcomes, but that the association was partially explained by psychosocial characteristics, and that there were additional unexplained pathways by which trauma affected health and behavior.

the effects of childhood trauma and the role of psychosocial mediates on health outcomes.
the relationship between childhood trauma (CT), defined as the experience of physical, emotional, and/or sexual abuse, and the development of chronic diseases later in life, particularly HIV/AIDS.
the impact of childhood trauma on the health of people living with HIV, and the pathways through which this effect occurs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
childhood trauma increases the risk of adverse health outcomes and behaviors in HIV infected individuals and that this association is only partially mediated by psychosocial factors.

childhood trauma is associated with a wide variety of health and behavioral outcomes in HIV-infected patients and this association is only partially explained by psychosocial mediates such as coping style, self-efficay, social support, and trust in the medical systems.
trauma has an effect on health and behaviors, but we don't know what that effect is.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
trauma is associated with worse health outcomes, but that the mechanisms by which trauma influences these outcomes are not yet understood.
trauma is associated with a wide range of negative health and behavioral outcomes, and this relationship is not explained by a set of well-studied psychosocial characteristics.

the effects of childhood adversity on health and behaviors may be more complex than previously understood.
trauma has important effects on health and health-related behaviors that are independent of psychosocial mediational pathways.
